questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That they had a good program for my study, and interesting courses

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
There was a mix up with my modules, so I was not signed up for any modules at first which was unfortunate. 
But once I met my tutor it all got sorted fairly quickly. I did however only receive a message that I was accepted for the exchange 1 month before I had to leave, which was stressful wrt. finding accommodation, flight tickets, etc. 
I do think that all these mistakes were due to the UK leaving the EU, which made it so that there was no longer any staff left to deal with Erasmus exchange students

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a pickup at the airport, and some tours, etc. you could sign up for on the first days

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was very stressful that I was not signed up for any modules

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Yes, I just found accommodation via the university, which was very easy

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Glen Eyre and Highfield Hall are good choices. gle

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A bit expensive, but easy to get

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very difficult to get an overview over all the possible modules

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Since I weren't registered for anything when I arrived, I ended up just going to the student support center where they helped my register

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Student support center + tutor. There was no help before I arrived

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 3/4 of the courses I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Maybe call and get some help from the host university?

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
They were somewhat equivalent to the ones at home, but maybe with a slightly lower academic level. 
I think this is due to the master programme only being 1 year in the UK vs 2 years in DK

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was a lot more independent. So there were not many TA classes, and there wasn't that much focus on the more practical stuff at the start of the semester like solving problems, writing assignments, etc.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Evolution of Complexity, Data Mining, Natural Language Processing, and Biometrics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed Evolution of Complexity as I think the professor is great, and the subject is very interesting. It is also not like any of the courses that KU offer, so it was really nice that I got an opportunity to take it.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to buy a lot of stuff when I got here including a duvet, duvet cover, pots, pans, cutlery, etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: All of the food was more expensive than I anticipated

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Every kind of social club that you can think of is available: swimming, badminton, cricket, running, comedy, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend joining the cinema, as you can volunteer and then go see the movies for free. 
There are also activities every week that you can join (like free yoga, roller-skating, colour run, free picnic, etc), so it's worth keeping your eye out for that on the app

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
There are many things to see in the area. 
You could visit Bournemouth or Portsmouth, or go the Isle of Wight, or head into London. The beach in Southampton is also nice, and it's a nice walk to go to Netley. Southampton also has an airport, so we ended up going to Belfast for Skt. Patrick's Day

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I ended up mostly socialising with other exchange students by just saying yes to almost every social event the first couple of weeks

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People are very polite here, and not so direct, so that can be a bit difficult when dealing with issues

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I like how warm and welcoming everyone is - like I said before people are very polite

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Take advantage of all the free social events that the uni offers
2. Campus is really nice, so it's worth finding accommodation nearby
3. Plan your Easter holiday well. It's a great opportunity to go travelling, but remember that you will probably get a lot of course work that is due at the end of the holiday

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pick a nice accommodation. I got Wessex which is a bit far out, so maybe prioritise something closer.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the friends I made and the trips I went on

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The exam period and the course work leading up to it was tough

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
